## Project: Nikahcom.in— Matrimonial Advertising & Profile Sharing Website
Case study page (share this): https://bineeshs.vercel.app/project?slug=nikah-com
Live website (share only if asked to see it): https://www.nikahcom.in/
Source repository: https://github.com/happyweddingofficial/community-connect-hub
Technologies: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, SEO, WhatsApp Integration
Summary: A clean, trust-focused website for a matrimonial advertising and profile-sharing service in Kerala, with a transparent four-step process, clear policy pages, testimonials, an FAQ and WhatsApp-first contact.
Quick facts: Category: Matrimonial Advertising Website; Region: Malappuram · Kerala; Contact: WhatsApp-first; Frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite
Case study details: Nikah.com: Connecting Families with Respect, Privacy & Trust Nikahcom.inis a matrimonial advertising and profile-sharing service based in Malappuram, Kerala. I built its website to feel minimal, trustworthy and community-focused: a predominantly white, mobile-friendly design that families of every age group can read and act on without friction. The Goal The service is not a broker or matchmaking bureau, and the site had to say so clearly. Visitors needed to understand how profiles are received, prepared and shared, what the service does and does not do, and how to reach the team, all without feeling like they were using a complicated portal. What I Built - Home page with a clear value proposition, a visible "not a broker" notice and highlights on privacy, direct family connection and genuine enquiries. - Four-step "How Our Service Works" flow: profile submission, review and preparation, promotion and sharing, and direct family connection. - Principles and advertising policy sections covering independent verification, no outcome guarantees and how subscription fees work. - Testimonials and FAQ sections that answer common questions about the service, verification, subscriptions and profile removal. - WhatsApp-first contact: join and enquiry buttons throughout the site open WhatsApp with a pre-filled message. - Dedicated pages: About Us, Terms & Policy, Privacy Policy and Contact Us, with a footer linking to profile removal requests and social channels. SEO & Discoverability The site ships with canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter metadata, geo tags for Malappuram, Kerala and keyword-focused descriptions for local matrimonial searches. The aim: a respectful, transparent site that explains the service honestly and makes the next step a single tap away. Tech Stack - React with TypeScript, built and bundled with Vite - Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui-style reusable components - Optimised WebP images and responsive layouts - Deployed on Vercel

## Project: Fitaval — Multi-Tenant Fitness Business Platform
Case study page (share this): https://bineeshs.vercel.app/project?slug=fitaval
Live website (share only if asked to see it): https://www.fitaval.com/
Technologies: Flutter, Dart, React, JavaScript, Mobile App, Web CRM, Multi-Tenant, Role-Based Access
Summary: A complete fitness-business ecosystem: a member mobile app, a gym management CRM and a super-admin console, giving gym owners, staff, trainers and platform operators one connected system.
Quick facts: Category: Fitness SaaS Platform; Surfaces: Mobile App · Gym CRM · Super Admin; My Role: Co-founder & CTO; Model: Multi-tenant, role-based
Case study details: Fitaval: One Platform for the Whole Fitness Business Fitaval is a multi-tenant fitness club management platform I co-founded and lead as CTO . It replaces the patchwork of disconnected tools gyms rely on with a single connected system for owners, staff, trainers, members and the platform team itself. The Problem Gyms typically run member records, attendance, subscriptions, payments, staff schedules and reviews in separate tools. Owners lack a clear picture, front-desk teams repeat work, and onboarding a new gym is slow. Three Connected Surfaces - Member mobile app: onboarding, sign-in, discovery, memberships, profile, notifications and settings, built mobile-first for Android and iOS. - Gym management CRM: dashboard metrics, member and attendance monitoring, plans and pricing, subscriptions, payments and finance views, staff and trainer records, and review management. - Super-admin console: gym registration review and verification, multi-gym oversight, payout and settlement management, and audit and security visibility. A unified sign-in portal routes each person to the right experience for their role. Who It Serves - Gym owners: run the business from one dashboard. - Front-desk staff: check attendance and assist onboarding. - Trainers: manage profiles, schedules and assignments. - Platform administrators: verify gyms and oversee the network. What Makes It Hard Several gyms share one platform, so every role and tenant boundary has to be precise. Subscriptions, wallets, payments and attendance must stay consistent with each other, and the product has to feel simple to a gym owner while carrying a lot of business logic underneath. The goal is not another gym app. It is a business operating system for fitness. My Role As co-founder and CTO I own product architecture, engineering delivery and the technical roadmap across the mobile app and web platforms.

## Project: CorePro Sales Hub — Sales CRM Platform
Case study page (share this): https://bineeshs.vercel.app/project?slug=corepro-sales-hub
Technologies: TanStack Start, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Firebase, Firestore, Recharts, Zod
Summary: A role-based sales CRM for CorePro Techno: lead management with CSV/Excel import, monthly target tracking for sales executives, and a live team dashboard for managers and admins.
Quick facts: Category: Internal Sales CRM; Roles: Admin · Sales Manager · Sales Executive; Frontend: TanStack Start + React 19; Backend: Firebase / Firestore
Case study details: CorePro Sales Hub: Sales CRM Platform for Growing Teams CorePro Sales Hub is the internal CRM built for CorePro Techno . Small sales teams usually juggle spreadsheets, chat threads and memory; this project replaces that with one fast workspace where leads, follow-ups and monthly targets live together. The Problem Managers had no real-time view of who was on track, executives had no single place for their assigned leads, and target progress was tallied by hand at the end of each month. What I Built - Three-level access hierarchy: Administrator, Sales Manager and Sales Executive, each seeing only what their role needs. Executives work their own leads; managers see the whole team. - Lead management: add leads manually or bulk-import from CSV/Excel, assign them to executives, move them through pipeline stages and log follow-ups. - Automatic target tracking: managers set monthly targets per executive; progress updates by itself as leads are marked won, with an "Achieved" state once the target is met. - Team dashboard: charts and tables showing pipeline health, conversion and which executives are ahead or behind. - Team module: create and manage users and roles from inside the app. Design Approach The interface is built for speed and clarity: a single sidebar shell, sortable tables, clear empty states and coloured status badges so a stage or target state can be read at a glance. A complete, role-based sales workspace: leads, targets and team performance in one place. Tech Stack - TanStack Start, TanStack Router and React Query on React 19 with TypeScript - Tailwind CSS with Radix UI primitives - Firebase / Firestore with security rules and a seed script - Spreadsheet import with SheetJS, validation with Zod, charts with Recharts

Features - Crop library: ideal growing conditions, fertiliser split-dosing, water needs and harvest periods for cereals, pulses, fruits and cash crops, seeded from a structured catalogue. - Prediction history so logged-in users can review past recommendations. - Roles: Farmer and Administrator profiles; admins can retrain the model from within the app. - Feedback and support form to reach the administrators. - Seed scripts that populate the database with standard crop profiles. ## Project: Cervical AI — Federated Learning Cancer Screening
Case study page (share this): https://bineeshs.vercel.app/project?slug=cervical-ai
Source repository: https://github.com/Bineesh627/cervical_ai
Technologies: Python, Django, PyTorch, Federated Learning, Explainable AI
Summary: A privacy-preserving multimodal AI system utilizing PyTorch models and the Flower federated learning framework for early cervical cancer detection.
Quick facts: CLASSIFICATION: PRIVACY_PRESERVING_AI; ML_ENGINE: PyTorch & Flower (FL); EXPLAINER: SHAP & Grad-CAM
Case study details: Cervical Cancer Detection with Federated Learning An advanced, privacy-preserving Multimodal AI System designed for the early detection and risk assessment of cervical cancer. By fusing clinical data (such as age, medical history, and smoking habits) with Pap smear image features, the system delivers high-accuracy diagnostic supports. Crucially, the project integrates Federated Learning (FL) to ensure absolute patient data privacy. The Challenge Early cervical cancer screening in low-resource environments suffers from a shortage of medical specialists. While centralized machine learning models can help, patient records and medical images are highly sensitive. Moving raw clinical data and medical scans to a centralized server raises severe privacy concerns, regulatory compliance issues, and data security risks. The Solution We engineered a decentralized system combining a Django web dashboard with PyTorch models and the Flower (flwr) federated learning framework. AI models train locally on client environments (hospitals/clinics), sending only updated model parameters to a central FL server rather than raw data. The application also integrates Explainable AI (XAI) tools—specifically Grad-CAM for image heatmaps and SHAP for clinical feature weights—to give clinicians transparent, interpretable diagnostic recommendations. Key Features - Multimodal Analysis: Synthesizes tabular clinical histories and digital cell imagery using feature fusion models to boost detection accuracy. - Federated Learning (FL): Uses Flower to execute privacy-preserving, distributed model training across client nodes without transferring raw data. - Explainable AI (XAI): Produces Grad-CAM overlays to highlight visual anomalies on Pap smear scans and SHAP plots to explain the impact of clinical metrics. - Role-Based Access Control: Distinct user paths for patients (to submit symptoms, upload scans, view predictions, and ask questions) and doctors (to review patient records, analyze XAI metrics, and answer questions). - Secure Web Console: Integrated Django application containing session controls, administrative logs, database state management, and real-time outputs. Technology Stack - Backend Framework: Django (Python) - Machine Learning: PyTorch, Torchvision - Federated Learning: Flower (flwr) - Image Processing: OpenCV, Pillow - Explainability (XAI): SHAP, Grad-CAM (pytorch-gradcam) -…

## Project: RAG Chatbot — AI College Assistant

Quick facts: CLASSIFICATION: OPEN_SOURCE; DATABASE_ENGINE: ChromaDB; NLP_FRAMEWORK: Langchain
Case study details: RAG Chatbot: Context-Aware College Assistant This case study explores the development of an intelligent query resolver developed for academic institutions. By utilizing advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, the chatbot extracts, sanitizes, and presents context-grounded information to students, faculty, and visitors directly from institutional web archives and PDF records. The Challenge Academic databases and institutional portals contain scattered documents (circulars, course catalogs, exam timetables) making it difficult for users to resolve routine queries instantly, placing a heavy load on support desks. The Solution We implemented a Langchain-driven ingestion engine that indexes documents into vector spaces. Coupled with local Ollama LLMs and integrated with a Django-based admin panel, it supports real-time source citations and system dashboard management. Key Technical Components - Vector Ingestion Pipeline: Dynamic indexing of PDF schedules and HTML scraping scripts. - Context-Grounded Generation: Prompt layouts structured to prevent LLM hallucinations. - Admin Dashboard: Diagnostic panel to audit queries and fine-tune ingestion indices. - Source Citation: Highlights exact file pathways and text contexts used to build answers. "Moving search queries from standard indexing to vector semantic search reduced repetitive student support tickets by 60% within the initial semester of pilot execution."

## Project: TruthGuard — LSTM-Based Fake News Detector

Quick facts: FRAMEWORK: Django 4.2; ALGORITHM: LSTM Neural Network; DATABASE: SQLite 3; FRONTEND: Bootstrap 5 & Tailwind
Case study details: TruthGuard: LSTM-Based Fake News Detector TruthGuard is a robust, full-stack Django web application designed to combat misinformation by performing real-time fake news detection on text inputs and URLs. Powering this platform is a deep learning LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural network that classifies articles with high accuracy, backed by a comprehensive user ecosystem, community feedback/voting mechanisms, and an advanced administration dashboard. The Challenge The rapid dissemination of misinformation online makes manual verification impossible. Modern fake news spreads virally, requiring automated, intelligent systems that can process arbitrary text or parse articles via URLs, analyze their deep sequential and semantic patterns in real-time, and adapt to community corrections to improve classification over time. The Solution We engineered a web application using Django 4.2 integrated with a TensorFlow/Keras LSTM neural network. Users can paste text or submit URLs for instant analysis, receiving a credibility label along with a confidence score. The platform incorporates user authentication, community-driven voting on predictions, a structured correction submission framework, and an active administration panel for monitoring logs and managing retraining pipelines. Key Technical Components - LSTM Neural Network: A deep learning classifier built with TensorFlow and Keras, utilizing custom tokenization, sequence padding, and joblib/pickle serialization for highly precise sequential text classification. - Django Web Framework: Provides robust backend routing, session-based user authentication, database models (Predictions, Votes, Feedback, ActivityLogs), and SQLite integration. - Interactive Frontend: Uses Bootstrap 5 and Tailwind CSS for utility-first styling, Lucide Icons, and SweetAlert2 for beautiful, responsive alerts and status popups. - Community-Driven Validation: Enables users to vote (Up/Down) on predictions and submit correction feedback to flag false predictions. - Admin Dashboard: A comprehensive diagnostic dashboard for system stats, user management, activity log tracking, feedback review, and data export. Artificial intelligence is transforming the digital world, creating new opportunities for innovation while introducing increasingly sophisticated cybersecurity threats. From AI-generated fake identities to deepfake videos and phishing attacks, online scams are becoming harder to identify. Addressing these growing challenges, COREPRO TECHNO LLP and RedSpector came together to present Stop the Scam , an AI Safety & Defense Workshop focused on improving cybersecurity awareness and helping people understand the evolving landscape of digital threats. Stop the Scam: Building Awareness Against Digital Threats The Stop the Scam initiative focuses on an important question: how can individuals and businesses protect themselves in an era where artificial intelligence can be used to manipulate digital information? The workshop was designed around practical cybersecurity awareness, helping participants understand common online threats, recognise suspicious digital activities, and develop safer technology practices. Rather than treating cybersecurity as only a technical subject, the initiative highlights why digital safety should be an essential skill for everyone. Four Key Areas of Focus The workshop highlighted four important areas of AI safety and cybersecurity. 1. AI Morphing Detection AI-powered image manipulation and identity morphing can be used to create misleading digital content. Understanding how manipulated images and identities are generated is an important step towards recognising potentially fraudulent activities. 2. Phishing Scam Prevention Phishing remains a common method used by cybercriminals to steal sensitive information. Participants were introduced to the importance of identifying suspicious messages, fraudulent links, impersonation attempts, and deceptive online communication. 3. Deepfake Identification AI-generated videos, images, and audio can make it increasingly difficult to distinguish authentic content from manipulated media. Understanding deepfake technology and recognising possible signs of manipulation are essential for developing better digital awareness. 4. Data Security Best Practices Protecting personal and organisational information…

Achieving this rank requires consistent practice, physical fitness, mental focus, and a dedication to mastering the principles of traditional karate. ## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is your typical freelance project workflow?
A: I follow a strict cybernetic execution path: 1) System analysis & spec discovery, 2) Rapid prototyping of core modules, 3) High-performance coding & secure integration, and 4) Production deployment with rigorous automated stress tests.
Q: Which programming languages and frameworks do you use?
A: My system stack centers on Python (Django, FastAPI, PyTorch, OpenCV, Scrapy) and JavaScript (React, Node.js). I also deploy using cloud VMs, Docker containers, and database layers (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Supabase).
Q: How do you handle project privacy and security?
A: Security is non-negotiable. All codebase repositories, API keys, credentials, and scraped datasets are guarded behind isolated env systems, encrypted channels, and local staging instances before deployment.
Q: Are you available for contract-based long-term hire?
